title: 《高等微積分》第 56 集｜度量空間、開集與閉集｜Loomis & Sternberg 第 4 章 §1
description:
本集是 Loomis 與 Sternberg《Advanced Calculus》第 4 章第 1 節（書頁 195 到 200）。書頁 200 到 201 是習題 1.1 到 1.15。

第 4 章從度量空間開始。前面三章談收斂與連續時，其實只用到「兩點之間的距離」這件事。把它抽出來就是三條公理：不同點的距離為正、對稱、以及三角不等式。賦範空間用範數當距離就是度量空間，而它的任何子集也是——從一個漂亮的空間裡挖一個奇怪的子集出來，得到的度量空間可以非常古怪。度量也不是只有範數這一種：球面上可以取大圓的長度，更一般地任何光滑曲面可以取曲面內最短曲線的長度。

定義照搬：連續是給了 ε 就有 δ，半徑 r 的球是離中心小於 r 的點，一個集合是開的如果它裡面每一點都是某個含在裡面的球的中心。引理 1.1 說每個球都是開的，證明就是三角不等式。定理 1.1 列出開集族的三條性質，推論是：一個集合是開的等價於它是一堆開球的聯集。

接下來一組互補的定義：內部是最大的開子集，閉集是補集為開的集合，閉包是最小的閉超集，邊界是閉包減去內部。有一個很好用的刻畫：一點落在閉包裡等價於它周圍每個球都跟那個集合相交。書上提醒，隨手拿一個集合通常既不開也不閉。

引理 1.4 把連續性翻成集合的語言：開集的逆像是開的，閉集的逆像是閉的，而且兩個的反面也成立。可是正像不保持——反正切函數的像是開區間；換一個更公平的例子，二 x 除以一加 x 平方的值域是閉區間，可是正整數這個閉集的像不閉，因為零在它的閉包裡。

兩個集合之間的距離取點對點距離的下確界。不相交也可能是零：圓的內部與外部是不相交的開集，x 軸與一除以 x 的圖形是不相交的閉集，兩對的距離都是零。

最後是引理 1.5，以及它為什麼不能改進：無窮維時最近的點可能根本不存在。

title: Advanced Calculus, Episode 56 | Metric Spaces, Open and Closed Sets | Ch. 4, §1
description:
This episode is section 1 of chapter 4, pages 195 to 200, of Loomis and Sternberg's Advanced Calculus. Pages 200 to 201 are exercises 1.1 to 1.15.

Chapter 4 begins with metric spaces. Everything the last three chapters did with convergence and continuity used only the distance between two points. Distilled, that is three axioms: positive for distinct points, symmetric, and the triangle inequality. A normed space is a metric space under the norm distance, and so is any subset of one — carve a weird subset out of a nice space and the result can be very odd indeed. Metrics come from elsewhere too: a sphere can use the great-circle distance, and any smooth surface the length of the shortest curve inside it.

The definitions carry over: continuity is the epsilon-delta one, a ball is the points nearer than r to its centre, and a set is open if every point of it centres a ball inside it. Lemma 1.1 says every ball is open, by the triangle inequality. Theorem 1.1 lists three properties of the family of open sets, and the corollary is that a set is open exactly when it is a union of open balls.

Then a complementary set of definitions: the interior is the largest open subset, a set is closed when its complement is open, the closure is the smallest closed superset, and the boundary is the closure minus the interior. One characterisation is very usable: a point lies in the closure exactly when every ball about it meets the set. The book warns that a set picked at random is generally neither open nor closed.

Lemma 1.4 restates continuity in the language of sets: inverse images of open sets are open and of closed sets closed, and both converses hold. Forward images do not behave — the range of the arctangent is an open interval; and for a fairer example, two x over one plus x squared has a closed range, yet the image of the positive integers is not closed, since zero lies in its closure.

The distance between two sets is the greatest lower bound of the point distances. Disjoint sets can be at distance zero: the inside and outside of a circle are disjoint open sets, the axis and the graph of one over x disjoint closed ones, and both pairs are at distance zero.

Finally Lemma 1.5, and why it cannot be improved: in infinite dimensions a nearest point may simply fail to exist.
